beats.trigger: Three agents search Confluence, OneDrive and practitioner articles, and three more decide what it means.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the message first and sends only after approval.
beats.got: The agent can act in another system, and the demo is built so it asks first and stops when unsure.

beats.trigger: Push back when the first answer restates the problem.
beats.got: The agent can read my earlier notes and name the core problem. Its first answer is probably generic, so I have to push it.

beats.trigger: If an agent starts reading the world, stop it, steer narrower, then say *"continue"*.
beats.got: Three sessions each pull from a different source, and I steer them like juniors. It reads like real work, and it is something I could test myself.

beats.trigger: You can't yet tell if the answer is right. That is expected.
beats.got: It admits plainly that I cannot yet tell whether the synthesis is correct. I appreciate that.

beats.trigger: When do you split, and how?
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A hundred tiny agents cost more to coordinate than they save.
beats.got: One agent per recurring job. Not too big, not too small. Sounds like org design for software.

beats.trigger: If one agent can produce what you need, use one.
beats.got: The training tells me not to build the complicated thing by default. No other transformation programme has said that to me.

beats.trigger: A backward planner and a reframer in the same voice are one agent pretending to be two.
beats.got: Three tests for splitting: access, dialect, stance. Clear and usable, and I could apply it to a team too.

beats.trigger: More input does not fix a beige answer.
beats.got: More agents does not mean more rigour. A sceptic can agree with that.

beats.trigger: The synthesizer then commits to one diagnosis and drops what does not serve it.
beats.got: Without a framework the AI averages the views; with one it has to choose. That matches every committee I have sat on.

beats.trigger: Could one prompt produce the same quality of output?
beats.got: A test for whether the multi-agent setup is just theatre.

beats.trigger: Each helper gets one job, reports back as a file and disappears.
beats.got: Two modes: long-lived sessions, or short-lived helpers inside one session. Technical detail I would hand to someone else.

beats.trigger: One agent can call another for a different stance, source zone, or working style.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A retriever finds two numbers and the curator keeps one.
beats.got: Handoffs lose information, and the example is exactly how it goes wrong in my own organisation.

beats.trigger: If one well-prompted agent does the job, write that prompt.
beats.got: nothing new. It repeats the earlier point.

beats.trigger: Agents get stuck: wrong source, three views averaged into mush, the wrong file written, confident right before a failed handoff.
beats.got: The module lists failure modes up front. That is candour about what does not work yet.

beats.trigger: Prompt your stuck system to diagnose whether the bug lives in the sources, the processing, or the boundary between agents.
beats.got: Ask the system where the fault is before fixing anything. Sensible, and a bit like root-cause analysis.

beats.trigger: move the risky step from "do" to "propose."
beats.got: Three places a fault can be, and a fix for each. 'Do' to 'propose' is a useful control idea.

take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only when the access, the source language or the stance differs. The training says this itself.
If you tell the AI to apply a framework, it has to pick a diagnosis instead of averaging views.
Problems appear in the handoffs between agents. The check does not tell you whether the result is true.

monday.blocker: A full calendar, and I have not seen the result of the crux exercise on a real problem of mine.

misconception.why: Nobody oversold it. It said 'use one agent' and 'the doubt stays', and that is not the usual transformation pitch. I do not think it will blow over, but I am not convinced yet. I still wait and see.

one_line: Fewer slogans than I expected. They tell you to use one agent first and admit they cannot yet say whether the answer is right. I do not know yet if the thing works.
